messages:
Alex: Heads-up — env-parity-monitor just flagged a parity alert between staging and prod for GPU pools. Prod has an extra nodepool named "shadow-gpu" (4 x a100). Terraform CI is blocking any plan because of a policy check. Anyone oncall?
InfraBot: [automated] parity-check FAILED: staging != prod. Diff: prod has "shadow-gpu" not present in staging. Blocking reason: tf-plan-policy-labels. See: https://ci.internal/parity/1712349876
Mai: that was my manual hotfix last week to handle a customer burst. I patched prod directly to add the pool, forgot to update gitops. sorry.
Sam: manual changes + autoscaler = bad combo. Requests are being routed to shadow-gpu which has different taints/labels; autoscaler thinks capacity is separate and we price-spiked.
Alex: logs show repeated scale-ups around 03:12 and leftover taint errors: "node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeSelector". snippet: `FailedScheduling: 0/8 nodes are available: 4 node(s) had taint {gpu-reserved: true}, 4 node(s) didn't match nodeSelector.`
Nina: could the policy gate be a false positive? We bumped the terraform k8s provider last month and label normalization changed (old key `gpu-type` -> new key `gpu.model`). Gitops expects old key so the policy check sees an unknown label.
Mai: yep — I applied `kubectl apply -f` from my laptop using the cluster labels I saw, which were the newer format. Git repo still has old schema.
Sam: quick repro I ran: `kubectl get nodepool shadow-gpu -o yaml` shows labels: `gpu.model: a100, gpu.count: 4, infra.team: ml`. Gitops expects `gpu-type` and `gpu-count`.
Alex: Proposed mitigation plan: 1) create an emergency GitOps PR to add shadow-gpu to infra repo (keeps congruence), 2) add temporary policy-check exception for both label keys, 3) schedule a graceful reconcile + canary to avoid draining traffic during peak. Thoughts?
Mai: Agree. I'll open the PR to add the pool to gitops with a short explanation and a retain-annotation so it doesn't get removed immediately. I'll also add a note to the runbook.
Nina: Also recommend updating the policy-check mapping so it accepts both `gpu-type` and `gpu.model` for 2 weeks. Then follow up with a provider/infra schema migration.
Sam: Cost note: 4 x a100 is approx ~$45/hr each (our internal list) => ~ $180/hr extra while the pool exists. If this is sustained we should convert to reserved or move load.
Alex: Can we avoid full drain? Propose adding a canary annotation to the gitops resource: `reconcile.canary=10%` then reconcile in low-traffic window.
Mai: I'll include the canary annotation in the PR and set a 2h auto-scale-down via a cronjob in the same PR. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/4387
InfraBot: [automated] Opened incident-ish thread: incident-#4632, linked PR https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/4387.
Sam: LGTM, approving PR now. I'll trigger `flux reconcile kustomization infra -n flux-system` after merge.
Nina: I'll add the temporary policy exception: patch `policy-check` with mapping rule to accept both keys and add an audit log entry.
Alex: Also adding a detector to alert on cluster-scoped `kubectl apply` outside of GitOps (simple webhook + query of audit logs), so future manual patching gets a pager.
Mai: PR merged and canary reconcile started. Link: https://ci.internal/flux/reconcile/1712349999
InfraBot: [automated] Reconciler kicked by Sam at 1712350000. Status: in-progress.
Sam: Reconciler finished at 1712350030 — shadow-gpu resource now managed in gitops and annotated with canary. No full drain.
Alex: Cost normalized in monitoring; autoscaler drift decreased. I'll mark this as action item to schedule provider label migration and update runbook.
Nina: Adding follow-ups: update provider version bump ticket, policy-check migration RFC, and reserve-sizing review for GPU pools.
Mai: Thanks all — sorry for the scramble. Lesson learned: always update infra repo when doing emergency fixes.
Sam: Closing loop — I'll keep an eye on billing dash for next 48h. :thumbsup:
